title: How many flowers bloom each day on a plant?
description: A flowering plant is watched for a week and the new flowers are counted each day. The board uses sample counts to add them, divide by seven days, and check the answer.
teaching_notes: One idea: record all seven daily counts first, then add them and divide by the number of days. Watch for students who average only the days on which flowers bloomed and leave out a day with none.

video_script.why: The child has found the average number of flowers per day from given counts and now has to collect counts for a plant and do the same.
video_script.substitution: Your own seven daily counts replace the given counts, and seven days replace five.
video_script.anchor: A flowering plant and a notebook with a count of flowers for each of seven days
video_script.payoff_line: The sample average is four flowers per day

final_answer.value: Sample data gives 28 ÷ 7 = 4 flowers per day; your own answer depends on your plant
final_answer.spoken: the sample data gives twenty eight divided by seven, which is four flowers per day, and your own answer depends on your plant

maths_rules: your own data: new flowers counted each day for a week, so 7 counts
average = total / number of days = 28 / 7 = 4 flowers per day
video_script.design: A plant and a notebook of seven days. Sample counts are added, shared over the seven days and multiplied back. A note says to record all seven counts before calculating.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a flowering plant beside a notebook with seven day rows

marks.m1: the title card From your book appears
marks.m3: the notebook with seven day rows appears
marks.m4: a question mark rises over the notebook

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>It asks you to pick a flowering plant in your neighbourhood.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>You count the flowers that bloom each day for a week.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>How will you find the average number of flowers per day?

beats.on_screen: the plant and the notebook stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child who is thinking

beats.on_screen: the notebook rows fill with sample counts and carry the label sample data

marks.g1: the seven rows fill with sample counts
marks.g2: the label sample data appears on the notebook

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>Your plant will give you its own counts.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>Here we use sample data to show the steps, the same way as the example in your book.

marks.given: the seven sample counts are written in a row

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the sample flowers on seven days are three, five, four, six, two, five and three.

beats.on_screen: To find: the average number of flowers per day

marks.find: the words average and per day are underlined

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the average number of flowers per day.

marks.s1: the seven counts are added one after another

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, add the flowers of all seven days to get the total.
<bookmark mark='s2'/>Three plus five plus four plus six plus two plus five plus three makes twenty eight.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, average = total ÷ number of days: 28 ÷ 7 = 4

marks.d1: the rule average = total ÷ number of days is written

narration: <bookmark mark='d1'/>Step two, divide the total by the number of days.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>Twenty eight divided by seven gives four.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, check: 4 × 7 = 28, the same as the total; with your own plant record all 7 counts first

marks.c1: the 4 is repeated across the 7 days
marks.c2: the product 28 is matched with the total

narration: <bookmark mark='c1'/>Step three, check by putting the answer back.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>Four multiplied by seven is twenty eight, which is the total.
With your own plant, write all seven counts before you calculate.

beats.on_screen: Answer: sample data gives 28 ÷ 7 = 4 flowers per day; your own answer depends on your plant
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The sample average is four flowers per day.
Your own answer will depend on your plant.
